title: BIM interoperability standardized late: IFC became ISO 16739 in 2013 and the ISO 19650 process standard arrived in 2018
content:
Standards history relevant to any construction data product (Wikipedia excerpt in the BIM briefing):

- BIM as a concept dates to the **1970s**; it only became an agreed term in the early 2000s
- **IFC** (Industry Foundation Classes, by buildingSMART) became international standard **ISO 16739 in 2013**
- UK BIM process standards (from 2007) formed the basis of **ISO 19650**, launched December **2018**
- **OpenBIM** (buildingSMART initiative) promotes vendor-neutral exchange on IFC, plus **BCF** for issue tracking and **IDS** (Information Delivery Specification) for defining model requirements
- **COBie** (2007, US Army Corps of Engineers) captures equipment lists, warranties, spare parts, and maintenance schedules for the operations phase; British Standard BS 1192-4 (2014)
- Early precedent: **CIS/2** for structural steel (late 1990s)

The economic backdrop: a 2004 NIST report conservatively estimated **$15.8B lost annually** by the US capital-facilities industry to inadequate interoperability — fragmentation, paper-based practices, inconsistent standardization. Interoperability pain is not incidental to construction; it is quantified, chronic, and the reason open standards (and products that compose with them) win.
description: BIM dates to the 1970s but standards came slowly: IFC (ISO 16739, 2013), ISO 19650 (2018), OpenBIM's BCF + IDS, COBie for handover. NIST put interoperability losses at $15.8B/yr in 2004.
